**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 7.6**

§ 7.6 requires Customer to pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as liquidated damages for *any* dependency delay — no materiality threshold, cure period, or aggregate limit. That directly contradicts the playbook position (no LDs or penalties payable by Customer) and nears the walk-away line, since ~40 days of delay would alone exhaust the mutual § 21.1 cap (12 months' Fees / USD 1,000,000).

No other Customer-payable LD or early-termination minimum exists in the Agreement (§ 27.3 confirms penalty-free termination for force majeure), so the fallback (3-month early-termination fee cap) is not needed here.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** replace the LD with excused Vendor performance plus an equitable adjustment to affected dates and schedules, and an express statement that Customer bears no liquidated damages or penalties for such delay — preserving Vendor's legitimate delay relief without a punitive payment.
